In the boundary case N=3, the inequalities give exactly the nine lattice points (2,2), (3,5), (3,6), (4,8), (4,9), (4,10), (5,13), (5,14), and (6,18); affine independence of the three Cayley vertices makes every Lambda_z a singleton, so every fiber is a translate of K, and the four equal-mass even-even fibers form a good class whose six unordered edges contribute 3 vol_3(K)/8, exactly as formula (11) prescribes. In general, grouping convex-combination coefficients proves the two inclusions in the exact Cayley representation, and every nonempty Lambda_z contributes a translate of the full-dimensional ball, so positive fiber volume is equivalent to membership in the base polygon. The adjacent-chord differences and the endpoint-chord difference have the stated nonnegative factorizations, giving precisely the lower and upper polygon boundaries. The Steiner formula uses the standard normalization vol_N(A+B_2^N)=sum_j kappa_{N-j} V_j(A), and homogeneity gives V_j(4 Lambda_z)=4^j V_j(Lambda_z), including lower-dimensional Lambda_z. Summing the canonical unordered edge weights gives the denominator 8 A_xi in (11) and the bound Q<=W_N/8.
